title: Erdős Problem #1165: Favourite Sites of Random Walks in ℤ²
description: How many sites share the maximum visit count of a 2D random walk infinitely often? Tóth (2001): at most 3. Hao-Li-Okada-Zheng (2024): exactly 3 almost surely. SOLVED.

meta.author: Erdős–Révész
meta.assumptions: 8 axioms: VisitCount and FavouriteSites (random walk infrastructure), prob_favourite_count_io with bounds (probability events), toth_favourite_sites_geq_4 (Tóth 2001), hao_li_okada_zheng_three_favourite_sites (Hao et al. 2024), bass_griffin_1d_unique (background). All theorems fully proved from axioms (0 sorries).

overview.historicalContext: This problem originates from Erdős and Révész's study of random walk visit frequencies, catalogued as Problem 6.77 in Vatter's 1999 collection. The question asks about the number of 'favourite sites' — positions achieving the maximum visit count — for a random walk in ℤ². In one dimension, Bass and Griffin (1985) showed the maximum is achieved at a unique site for large n. The two-dimensional case is fundamentally different due to the marginal recurrence of ℤ² random walks. Tóth (2001, Annals of Probability) proved the upper bound: at most 3 favourite sites infinitely often. The matching lower bound took 23 years: Hao, Li, Okada, and Zheng (2024) proved that exactly 3 favourite sites occur infinitely often, completely resolving the problem.
overview.problemStatement: Consider a simple random walk $s_0, s_1, \ldots$ in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ starting at the origin. Let $f_n(x) = |\{k \leq n : s_k = x\}|$ be the visit count of position $x$ at time $n$. Define $F(n) = \{x : f_n(x) = \max_y f_n(y)\}$ as the set of favourite sites. Find $\mathbb{P}(|F(n)| = r \text{ infinitely often})$ for $r \geq 3$.
overview.text: How many sites share the maximum visit count of a 2D random walk infinitely often? Answer: exactly 3 almost surely (Tóth 2001 + Hao-Li-Okada-Zheng 2024).
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization axiomatizes the random walk infrastructure (visit counts, favourite sites, probabilities of infinitely-often events) and states the two main results as axioms. The complete resolution theorem and derived consequences are proved from these axioms. The approach is necessarily axiomatic since Mathlib does not yet have the probabilistic machinery for 2D random walk local time analysis.
keyInsights: **Dimensional dichotomy**: In 1D, the favourite site is unique for large n (Bass-Griffin 1985). In 2D, the marginal recurrence allows multiple favourite sites, but the walk's diffusive behaviour limits this to exactly 3.

**23-year gap**: Tóth's 2001 upper bound (≤ 3) took over two decades to match with a lower bound (≥ 3, Hao et al. 2024), reflecting the extreme technical difficulty of proving that three-way ties persist.

**Marginal recurrence**: ℤ² random walks return to the origin with probability 1 but have infinite expected return time. This 'barely recurrent' behaviour is key: enough returns to create ties, but not enough for four-way ties to persist.

sections.title: Problem Statement and Context
sections.summary: Module docstring: the problem statement about favourite sites of 2D random walks, the complete resolution by Tóth (2001) and Hao-Li-Okada-Zheng (2024), and background on dimensional differences in favourite site behaviour.

sections.title: Random Walk Infrastructure
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the core objects: ℤ² lattice, visit count function, maximum visit count, and favourite sites as a Finset. These form the interface needed to state the problem.

sections.title: Probability Events
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the probability of the infinitely-often event for favourite site counts, with basic probability bounds (non-negative, at most 1).

sections.title: Main Results (SOLVED)
sections.summary: States the two axioms that resolve the problem: Tóth (2001) proves P = 0 for r ≥ 4, Hao-Li-Okada-Zheng (2024) proves P = 1 for r = 3.

sections.title: Derived Consequences
sections.summary: Three proved theorems: the complete resolution combining both results, the finite occurrence corollary for r ≥ 4, and the almost-sure three-favourite-sites theorem.

sections.title: Background Results
sections.summary: Bass-Griffin (1985) 1D uniqueness result, providing context for why the 2D case is fundamentally different.

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures Erdős Problem #1165, a solved problem about the number of favourite sites (positions with maximum visit count) for 2D random walks. The complete resolution shows exactly 3 favourite sites occur infinitely often almost surely, combining Tóth's 2001 upper bound with the 2024 lower bound by Hao, Li, Okada, and Zheng.
conclusion.implications: The resolution reveals a precise structural property of 2D random walks: the marginal recurrence of ℤ² allows exactly a three-way tie for the most-visited site to recur infinitely, but not a four-way tie. This connects to broader questions about the geometry of random walk local times and the fine structure of recurrence in different dimensions.
openQuestions: What is the analogous result for random walks in ℤ^d for d ≥ 3? (In d ≥ 3, the walk is transient, so the problem has a different character.)
Can the result be extended to other types of random walks (e.g., non-simple, continuous-time)?
What is the asymptotic behaviour of the sizes of near-maximum visit count sets?

references.title: No more than three favourite sites for simple random walk
references.note: Proves P(|F(n)| = r i.o.) = 0 for r ≥ 4 in the 2D random walk, establishing the upper bound of 3 favourite sites.

references.title: Three favourite sites occurs infinitely often for one-dimensional simple random walk
references.note: Proves P(|F(n)| = 3 i.o.) = 1, matching Tóth's upper bound and completely resolving Erdős Problem #1165.
